There are a lot of jobs that offer demonstrable proof that the work actually *helps* other humans.

Media feels like an entire industry where there is no such proof (sorry — clicks, likes & other attention metrics are not proof). 

Burnout happens when you lose faith that work has meaning. I think this is why a lot of non-narcissistic only-in-it-for-attention sociopaths end up burning out in media jobs, and go off to do work where proof of meaning and value is far more clear.

It is incredible to me that even here in 2026 — with the world on fire — there remains a not insignificant faction of liberals in America who are cool with powerful Democrats who they know say popular things but do not do even the bare minimum to actually DO those things.

There's a link between the mental health crisis & everyone plugging their cognition into algorithms telling you everyone else has better careers & richer, happier, more successful and fulling lives than you, who should feel shame at how pathetic you are in comparison.

Journalism becomes a soul-crushing bullshit job if you are reporting bullshit, or if you are reporting important stuff that can't be heard through the bullshit.

I have no sympathy for purveyors of the former. I have sympathy - but no answers - for practitioners of the latter.
